The United States reported four H5 (N untyped) outbreaks on 29 May 2026.

UOhMvpnkL1whfGFDTvNYMA.zh: 今年第19週(5/11-17)全球陽性率由低點略升至1.12%,其中,東南亞區署陽性率明顯增加。近期全球流行變異株以BA.3.2及XFG為主(各占37.5%),其次為NB.1.8.1(占21.88%)。 中國疫情於低點略升,第22週(5/25-31)門急診陽性率略升為2.1%,變異株以NB.1.8.1占大宗。 新加坡疫情於高點波動,第19-20週陽性率自16.67%再上升至18%,第21週則下降至13%,變異株以NB.1.8.1占大宗。
UOhMvpnkL1whfGFDTvNYMA.en: In week 19 (11–17 May), the global positivity rate rose slightly from its low point to 1.12%, with a marked increase in the WHO South-East Asia Region. Circulating variants are mainly BA.3.2 and XFG (each 37.5%), followed by NB.1.8.1 (21.88%). In China, the positivity rate at outpatient and emergency visits rose slightly to 2.1% in week 22 (25–31 May), with NB.1.8.1 accounting for most variants. In Singapore, positivity has fluctuated at a high level: it rose from 16.67% to 18% in weeks 19–20, then fell to 13% in week 21, with NB.1.8.1 the dominant variant.

qC-skWFWva8nuJiHyJyh5A.zh: 智利今年截至5/9累計報告41例病例及14例死亡,致死率為34%,高於2025年同期致死率18%(44例病例及8例死亡),以艾森大區之發生率為高,病毒型別為安第斯病毒。病例以男性為多(78%),年齡中位數為31歲,主要危險因子包含居住在鄉村地區、戶外活動或健行、農業或林業工作等。
qC-skWFWva8nuJiHyJyh5A.en: Chile has reported 41 cases and 14 deaths cumulatively this year as of 9 May, a CFR of 34%, higher than the 18% for the same period in 2025 (44 cases and 8 deaths). Incidence is highest in the Aysén Region, and the virus type is Andes virus. Men account for most cases (78%), with a median age of 31 years. Main risk factors include living in rural areas, outdoor activities or hiking, and agricultural or forestry work.

i3J2StgqBLGAjGsW80Lm0g.zh: WHO於5/13公布國際郵輪漢他病毒安地斯型群聚事件,迄共掌握11例病例(8例確診、2例極可能病例、1例確認中),其中3例死亡。郵輪撤離行動已在西班牙特內里費島(Tenerife)完成,計有120名人員下船,搭乘專機返國,並依照該國家規範進行隔離追蹤。目前郵輪上尚有27人 (25名船員、1名荷蘭醫師/護理師),刻正駛往荷蘭鹿特丹,預計5/17抵達。WHO建議高風險接觸者應自5/10起進行為期42天監測,並在指定機構內觀察、每天測量體溫及檢查症狀(如發燒、疲勞、肌肉酸痛、頭痛、胃腸道及呼吸道症狀)。WHO尊重各國隔離檢疫方式,惟強烈建議下船旅客在監測期間,倘須與其他人接觸,應佩戴高規口罩(如N95或FFP2),另避免在監測期內進行國內/外旅遊。WHO評估此事件對全球公共衛生風險為「低」,船上乘客與船員風險則評估為「中」。
i3J2StgqBLGAjGsW80Lm0g.en: On 13 May, WHO announced an Andes-type hantavirus cluster linked to an international cruise ship. A total of 11 cases have been identified (eight confirmed, two probable and one under investigation), of which three died. Evacuation of the cruise ship was completed at Tenerife, Spain: 120 people disembarked and flew home on charter aircraft, and were placed under isolation follow-up in line with national requirements. There are still 27 people on board (25 crew and one Dutch doctor or nurse), and the ship is heading to Rotterdam, the Netherlands, expected to arrive on 17 May. WHO recommends that high-risk contacts be monitored for 42 days from 10 May, observed at designated facilities, have their temperature measured daily and be checked for symptoms such as fever, fatigue, muscle pain, headache, and gastrointestinal and respiratory symptoms. WHO respects each country's quarantine approach but strongly recommends that disembarked passengers who must contact others during the monitoring period wear high-grade masks (such as N95 or FFP2) and avoid domestic or international travel during that period. WHO assesses the global public health risk from this event as low, and the risk to passengers and crew on board as moderate.

Me30Xd7LHiDaGQ8Bn7VbjA.zh: 疫情更新:  今年第 15 週(4/13-19)全球陽性率略降為 1.11%,其中西太平洋、東南亞、東地中海署陽性率明顯增加。 中國疫情於低點略增,第 18 週(4/27-5/3)門急診陽性率略升至1.5%,變異株以 NB.1.8.1 占大宗。 韓國疫情略降,第 18 週增加 40 例住院病例,疫情已連續 2 週下降,陽性率 2.8%,近期變異株占比以 NB.1.8.1 及 PQ.2 (均為34.6%)為主,其次為 BA.3.2(占 23.1%)。  評估與建議:  近期全球流行變異株 JN.1、NB.1.8.1、XFG 占比相當(皆為 26.15%),其次為 BA.3.2(占 20%)。WHO 公布 COVID-19 全球長期快速風險評估(第 9 版),評估對全球公共衛生的整體風險屬中等。鑑於自然感染與疫苗帶來的群體免疫力提升,以及臨床治療的進步,全球住院與死亡數自 2022 年以來明顯下降。 目前多數流行變異株為 Omicron JN.1 及其衍生亞型,雖具備免疫逃脫能力,惟不至於造成疾病嚴重度增加,然有 6%有症狀病例出現長新冠症狀;現階段尚未形成穩定季節性流行規律,多數國家已減少常規檢測通報,汙水與定醫監測成為重要的補充監測方式。 WHO 指出,目前疫苗仍能有效預防重症與死亡,並建議優先保護高風險族群、與流感疫苗共同施打;同時透過《冠狀病毒疾病威脅管理策略計劃》呼籲各國整合防治計畫,持續加強監測、保護高風險族群、維持醫療與公衛韌性,並落實風險溝通。
Me30Xd7LHiDaGQ8Bn7VbjA.en: Update: In week 15 (13–19 April), the global positivity rate fell slightly to 1.11%, with a marked increase in positivity in the WHO regional offices for the Western Pacific, South-East Asia and the Eastern Mediterranean. In China, the outbreak rose slightly from a low point, and outpatient and emergency positivity rose slightly to 1.5% in week 18 (27 April–3 May), with NB.1.8.1 accounting for most variants. In South Korea, the outbreak has declined slightly: hospitalised cases rose by 40 in week 18, and the outbreak has fallen for two consecutive weeks. Positivity was 2.8%, and recent variant shares were led by NB.1.8.1 and PQ.2 (each 34.6%), followed by BA.3.2 (23.1%). Assessment and recommendations: recently circulating variants JN.1, NB.1.8.1 and XFG account for similar shares (each 26.15%), followed by BA.3.2 (20%). WHO's COVID-19 Global Long-term Rapid Risk Assessment (9th edition) rates the overall risk to global public health as moderate. Given population immunity from natural infection and vaccination, and advances in clinical treatment, global hospitalisations and deaths have declined markedly since 2022. Most circulating variants are Omicron JN.1 and its descendant subvariants; although they can escape immunity, they do not appear to increase disease severity, although 6% of symptomatic cases have long COVID symptoms. No stable seasonal pattern has yet formed, and most countries have reduced routine testing and reporting, so wastewater and sentinel clinic surveillance have become important supplementary tools. WHO notes that vaccines remain effective at preventing severe disease and death, and recommends prioritising protection of high-risk groups and co-administration with influenza vaccines. WHO calls on countries to integrate prevention and control plans under its COVID-19 threat management strategic plan, continue strengthening surveillance, protect high-risk groups, maintain health system and public health resilience, and implement risk communication.

jVDI2MoiITemc93PDPGgzw.en: Epidemic update. Human cases: No new cases were reported this week. Avian and animal outbreaks (WAHIS): So far this year, 49 countries and regions have reported 2,188 high- and low-pathogenicity avian influenza outbreaks cumulatively. Fourteen countries reported 373 H5N1 outbreaks during 12–20 March 2026: Germany 286, the United States 39, Denmark 15, Poland 8, the Netherlands 7, Taiwan 4, Canada, Austria, Estonia, Cambodia, Lithuania and Montenegro 2 each, and Czechia and Japan 1 each. Peru reported 1 H5 (N untyped) outbreak on 14 March 2026. In the United States, avian influenza in dairy cattle has been reported in 19 states since March 2024, with 1,088 outbreaks cumulatively; recent cases are concentrated in Wisconsin and California. US wastewater surveillance provided results from 452 sampling sites for 8–14 March 2026, of which 8 sampling sites in Illinois, New Jersey, Oregon and California detected H5-positive results. Other updates: The ECDC, EFSA and IZSV jointly published an avian influenza surveillance report covering December last year to February this year. Across 32 European countries, 2,514 highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5) cases were reported, mostly in wild birds (2,108), followed by poultry (289) and captive birds (117). All detected viruses belong to the clade 2.3.4.4b lineage, and H5N1 predominates (99.7%). The epidemic peaked in November last year and has declined since the end of the wild bird winter migration, but the overall viral threat remains high. Mammalian infections show an increasing trend, mainly in wild animals such as red foxes and raccoons. The Netherlands has for the first time found serological evidence of possible spillover of wild-bird virus into dairy cattle, which may further affect the safety of the dairy supply chain. No human cases were reported in Europe during this period, but China and Cambodia reported 10 human infections, all related to direct contact with infected poultry. ECDC assesses the risk to the general population as 'low' and the risk to occupationally exposed groups as 'low to moderate'.

Authorities advise that anyone with suspected symptoms should first call a medical institution and follow its instructions for seeking care, avoid using public transport, and check whether they have been vaccinated on schedule.

7CBIlhUKV_i6t5fWPI7n_g.en: Honduras is experiencing a severe pertussis situation this year. Authorities urge that infants under 1 year old be brought in promptly to complete vaccination. The country reported 114 confirmed cases last year.

Eqntd7L3g2K9Y4gp_XrpeQ.en: WHO updated the global situation on 13 March. As of 25 February this year, 10 countries had reported 144 confirmed and suspected cases cumulatively. All patients fell ill after consuming infant formula of different brands. Investigation found the cause to be contamination of the arachidonic acid (ARA) oil supply chain. Products have been withdrawn from sale in 99 countries, and WHO assesses the overall public health risk of this event as moderate.

bcRqMjbw3PvZ1wjeB4UIXQ.zh: 哈薩克疫情持續,突厥斯坦州奇姆肯特新增1例75歲男性確診病例,於2/17住院治療中,奇姆肯特鄰近地區畜牧業盛行,為炭疽病高風險地區。

herrzLBvm2J8iIdeKGTk8Q.en: The US FDA reported 33 multistate foodborne outbreaks in 2025, with 921 cumulative cases. Common pathogens were Salmonella, E. coli and Listeria. Botulism contamination of infant formula has also drawn attention. Common contamination sources include eggs, ready-to-eat foods, vegetables, nut products, raw seafood such as oysters, and dairy products.

QSQ3SGl_00jPO15z3Bj_7A.zh: 越南2025年累計報告95例確定病例,較2024年增加74例,境內5血清型(A、B、C、W和Y)皆在流行,其中,C及W血清型會導致較高死亡率。另11月份即報告11例,北寧省、胡志明市等地已出現多起死亡病例。專家表示該疾病早期症狀不明顯,致許多病例未進行檢測,實際病例數可能高於官方統計,專家呼籲民眾應提高警覺及進行全面疫苗接種作業。
QSQ3SGl_00jPO15z3Bj_7A.en: Viet Nam reported 95 confirmed cases cumulatively in 2025, 74 more than in 2024. All five serogroups (A, B, C, W and Y) are circulating in the country, and serogroups C and W cause higher mortality. In November alone, 11 cases were reported, and several deaths have occurred in areas including Bac Ninh province and Ho Chi Minh City. Experts say early symptoms of the disease are not obvious, so many cases are not tested, and the actual number of cases may be higher than official statistics. Experts urge the public to raise their awareness and to get fully vaccinated.

p6gGTy1MS5s4x0x4Kte0fw.en: Situation update: global test positivity fell to 2.8% in week 50 of 2025 (8–14 December), though it rose in the African, American and European Regions. China is at a low level; test positivity was 0.7% in week 52 (22–28 December), the same as the previous week, and NB.1.8.1 is the most common recent variant. Hong Kong fluctuates at a low level; test positivity fell to 0.03% in week 52 of 2025. XFG is the variant with the largest share in wastewater surveillance, while NB.1.8.1 is the most common variant among mild cases. The United Kingdom's situation has declined: hospital admissions fell to 495 in week 51 of 2025 and test positivity fell to 1.6%, with the highest positivity among people aged 85 and over. Given that COVID-19 continues to spread widely and causes severe disease and deaths among high-risk groups, WHO's strategic plan for managing the threat of coronavirus disease calls on countries to integrate broader respiratory and other infectious disease prevention and control programmes, and to strengthen integrated, sustainable and evidence-based management of the coronavirus disease threat.

Overall activity in the southern hemisphere is low, although test positivity in some countries remains above 10%.

-zEDBSamoqkz8ivouyQG9Q.en: Monthly update: Since May 2022 and as of 31 October this year, 142 countries and areas have reported more than 169,000 confirmed cases, of which at least 446 died (CFR 0.26%). Year to date as of week 44, 98 countries and areas have reported more than 48,000 confirmed cases: more than 40,000 in the African Region, 3,653 in the Region of the Americas, 2,290 in the European Region, 1,355 in the Western Pacific Region, 118 in the South-East Asia Region and 44 in the Eastern Mediterranean Region. Cases have declined in Africa, the Americas, the Western Pacific and the Middle East, but risen in Europe and South-East Asia. Other updates: WHO reported that from 5 September to mid-October, excluding Central and East Africa, 21 clade Ib cases were newly reported across five WHO regions (details not listed), of which nine had no travel history to affected areas and at least five were in the MSM population. Malaysia, Namibia, the Netherlands, Portugal and Spain reported clade Ib cases for the first time. Belgium, Germany, Italy, Spain, Qatar and Canada reported travel-associated imported clade Ib cases, with travel to affected areas including Malaysia, Uganda, Angola, Kenya, Tanzania, Lebanon and the Middle East. In countries outside Central and East Africa, six countries (Italy, the Netherlands, Spain, Portugal, the United States and Malaysia) reported locally acquired cases with no travel history or known contact with a case, indicating undetected community transmission chains. Assessment and recommendations: WHO ended the Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) on 5 September. However, because different genotypes continue to circulate in Africa, surveillance and diagnostic capacity are insufficient, and funding and community resources are inadequate, WHO still assesses the global transmission risk as moderate. Because cases among asymptomatic infected people and travellers from affected areas were not detected promptly, clade Ib transmission risk persists. Italy, the Netherlands, Portugal, Spain and the United States, outside Africa, have been listed as clade Ib community transmission areas. This report resembles the early phase of 2022, with rapid spread through the MSM population, and a new generation that has not been vaccinated and has never been infected, creating an immunity gap. The assessed risk to the general public is low, but moderate for MSM, especially those without a stable sexual partner. Countries are advised to improve testing capacity and complete contact tracing, and high-risk individuals are urged to get vaccinated.

3m1yT-oJvl4EY90BnZEjeg.zh: WHO於10/13發布全球抗生素抗藥性監測報告,2023年全球經實驗室確診之細菌感染病例中,約有1/6對抗生素出現抗藥性,2018-23年間,監測抗生素中出現抗藥性比例超過40%,平均每年增幅介於5-15%間;各區署中以東南亞及東地中海區抗藥性最為嚴重,約1/3無法以現有抗生素治療。報告顯示,大腸桿菌/克雷伯氏肺炎桿菌(K. pneumoniae)對第三代頭孢菌素(cephalosporin)出現抗藥性的比例迄已分別達40%及55%,於非洲地區更超過70%,另碳青黴烯類(carbapenems)與氟喹諾酮類(fluoroquinolones)等效力也下降,使治療選擇逐漸受限。目前已有104國參與WHO 全球抗藥性與使用監測系統(GLASS),惟近半數未能提供可靠資料,呼籲各國於2030年前提高監測數據品質,強化實驗室系統與抗藥性防治。
3m1yT-oJvl4EY90BnZEjeg.en: On 13 October, WHO issued its global antibiotic resistance surveillance report. Of laboratory-confirmed bacterial infections worldwide in 2023, about one in six were resistant to antibiotics. Between 2018 and 2023, the proportion of resistance among monitored antibiotics exceeded 40%, with average annual increases of 5–15%. Among the regions, South-East Asia and the Eastern Mediterranean have the most serious resistance, with about one third of infections untreatable with existing antibiotics. The report shows that resistance to third-generation cephalosporins has reached 40% in Escherichia coli and 55% in Klebsiella pneumoniae, and more than 70% in the African Region. The effectiveness of carbapenems and fluoroquinolones has also declined, gradually limiting treatment options. Currently 104 countries participate in WHO's Global Antimicrobial Resistance and Use Surveillance System (GLASS), but nearly half cannot provide reliable data. WHO calls on countries to improve the quality of surveillance data by 2030, and to strengthen laboratory systems and antimicrobial resistance control.

RKHWJ-M1C2H9ebLvO63RGQ.en: WHO reports that globally, cumulative cases this year reached 210,000 as of May, with 2,754 deaths. Cases were distributed across 18 countries and territories in Africa, the Eastern Mediterranean and South-East Asia, with the highest prevalence in South Sudan, Afghanistan and Angola. The current global emergency stockpile of oral cholera vaccine averages 5.7 million doses, above the safe threshold of 5 million doses. WHO assesses the global transmission risk as very high.

CgSAh7s7k-3HV0e5QCPuCA.en: WHO held the 4th meeting of the IHR Emergency Committee on Mpox on 5 June. The global situation remains a PHEIC, and related recommendations have been extended to 20 August this year. The meeting noted that since 2024, 25 countries have reported more than 37,000 cases, including 125 deaths. African outbreaks remain severe, mainly in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, which reports 2,000–3,000 suspected cases weekly, followed by Uganda, Burundi and Sierra Leone. xcStAqDTYAZNw9wO2bayhA.zh: WHO於5/23將變異株NB.1.8.1列為監測中變異株(VUM),該變異株於全球占比漸升,第14週(3/31-4/6)至第17週(4/21-27)該變異株占比由2.5%上升至10.7%,截至5/18,共22國報告518筆序列,其中西太平洋/美洲/歐洲皆呈上升趨勢,其餘區署上傳序列數較低或無相關紀錄。NB.1.8.1變異株源於重組變異株XDV.1.5.1,首例於今年1/22樣本檢測出,現有證據顯示部分位點突變使病毒可增強與人體ACE受體結合能力,以提高傳播力,並降低抗體中和效力及增加免疫逃脫力,惟需更多實驗證據。目前西太平洋區該變異株比例較高之國家,其病例/住院數皆上升,惟無證據顯示其嚴重度高於其他變異株,目前已核准使用之疫苗,預期仍具有保護效力,評估對全球公衛風險為低。
xcStAqDTYAZNw9wO2bayhA.en: On 23 May, WHO designated the variant NB.1.8.1 as a variant under monitoring (VUM). Its share of global cases has been rising: from 2.5% in week 14 (31 March–6 April) to 10.7% in week 17 (21–27 April). As of 18 May, 22 countries had reported 518 sequences. The variant's share is rising in the Western Pacific, the Americas and Europe, while other regions have uploaded fewer sequences or have no relevant records. NB.1.8.1 derives from the recombinant variant XDV.1.5.1, and the first case was detected in a sample collected on 22 January this year. Current evidence suggests that some mutations may enhance the virus's binding to the human ACE receptor, potentially increasing transmissibility, reducing antibody neutralization and increasing immune escape, but more experimental evidence is needed. In Western Pacific countries where this variant accounts for a higher share, case and hospitalization numbers have risen, but there is no evidence that it causes more severe disease than other variants. Currently approved vaccines are expected to remain protective, and the global public health risk is assessed as low.

Avian and animal cases: 1,740 highly and low pathogenic avian influenza outbreaks have been reported cumulatively by 53 countries and regions. Assessment and recommendations: FAO, WHO and WOAH published a risk assessment on H5 influenza viruses on 17 April. Currently, H5 2.3.4.4b viruses are still avian viruses; most human cases had direct or indirect contact with susceptible animals, and no human-to-human transmission has occurred. Because the virus is widespread in wild and farmed animals, cases are expected to continue, and the global public health risk is assessed as low. Countries are urged to strengthen surveillance of susceptible animals and high-risk groups.

The virus continues to evolve and spread across species, but related research and surveillance remain underestimated, and the study recommends strengthening surveillance of mammals that have frequent contact with humans. In Camarines Sur Province in southeastern Luzon, the Philippines, HPAI H5N9 was detected in duck samples during routine surveillance; this is the first detection of this virus strain in the country. Local authorities have strengthened surveillance and disinfection and culled ducks on affected farms. Current assessment: H5N9 is highly pathogenic to birds, and the risk to humans is low. 0FSNy4__imGBIwgXJHG_fw.en: Epidemic update: in week 16 of 2025 (14–20 April), the global positivity rate was about 2.6%, highest in the Eastern Mediterranean, Western Pacific and Americas regions. In Hong Kong, positivity in week 18 (27 April–3 May) continued to rise and was the highest in the past 52 weeks; wastewater surveillance data show the XDV variant accounts for the largest share and is rising. Among countries in the South-East Asia Region, positivity in week 17 ranged from 0% to 4.8%, with Thailand the highest at 4.8%; the main circulating variant is XEC. Assessment and recommendations: global positivity has recently risen slightly. It has risen recently in the Eastern Mediterranean and Western Pacific regions, fluctuated in the South-East Asia and African regions, and remained flat or declined elsewhere. The main variants circulating globally are XEC, LP.8.1 and JN.1. WHO notes that most countries have incorporated COVID-19 into routine respiratory infectious disease surveillance, and recommends that countries provide affordable and trustworthy testing, treatment and vaccines, maintain early-warning surveillance systems and continue tracking variant trends, report epidemic information to WHO, and maintain the infrastructure established during the COVID-19 period.

FSYubJstQqrZIHxxLq6keQ.en: The European CDC (ECDC) reports that globally, as of 2 May this year, more than 111,000 cases have been reported cumulatively, of which about 1,500 died (CFR 1.4%). xNRhRjNCey2mVi-QYvNWmg.zh: 本週摘要:  人類疫情:本週新增越南1例H5N1流感、中國3例H9N2流感人類感染病例。 禽/動物疫情(WAHIS):共8國於2025/2/3-4/17期間新增33起H5N1疫情,匈牙利11起、德國/英國各7起、荷蘭3起、美國2起、羅馬亞/愛沙亞/賴比瑞亞各1起。 日本於2025/4/10新增3起H3N8疫情。  美國乳牛感染禽流感案:  乳牛場:去年3月迄今累計17州報告1,021 (14)起疫情,近期主要集中於愛達荷州、加州、內華達州及亞利桑那州。 人類經牛感染:累計監測至少9,300例,檢測218例,其中41例陽性(結膜炎、呼吸道及流感症狀)。 其他衍生疫情:感染家貓/羊/羊駝等,其中出現貓隻死亡案例。 廢水監測:第15週計351個採檢點提供檢測報告,其中,3州(加州、愛荷華、紐澤西)3個採檢點檢出H5陽性。  其他更新:  越南 4/18報告1例H5N1流感人類感染病例,為該國東南部西寧省邊求縣8歲女童,病患具先天心臟疾病史,4/11發病,出現發燒、頭痛、嘔吐等症狀就醫住院,因病況無改善於13日轉院,後出現嗜睡、頸部僵硬、精神意識異常等症狀,診斷為腦膜腦炎,17日腦脊髓液檢驗出H5流感陽性,18日H5N1流感確診,惟呼吸道檢體皆為陰性,病患目前仍於ICU進行治療,生命徵象暫穩定。據調查病患於發病前2週曾接觸病死家禽,相關調查持續進行。專家表示僅腦脊髓液檢出H5N1流感,呼吸道檢體陰性為罕見事件,該國曾於2004年報告過2例症狀相兒童,病患皆病況嚴重且死亡。 WHO更新墨西哥H5N1流感人類感染資訊,病患為該國西北部杜蘭戈州3歲女童,3/7出現發燒、嘔吐等症狀,3/13因呼吸衰住院,其後接受抗病毒藥物治療,於4/1確診,8日因呼吸併發症死亡。經檢驗感染D1.1基因型(屬2.3.4.4b分支),該基因型亦於美國及加拿大檢出,並報告5例人類感染病例,其中1例死亡。目前接觸者調查皆為陰性,該州近期無家禽疫情,惟今年迄今報告3起其他禽鳥H5流感案件。  年度摘要:  人類病例: H5N1流感10例 (2003年迄今累計973*例)、H9N2流感3例(迄今累計131例),個案發病前多有易感動物相關暴露史。(依WHO統計方式將美國H5流感病例列為H5N1流感病例。) 禽類/動物案例:累計50國家/地區通報1,557起高/低病原性禽流感疫情。  評估與建議: FAO/WHO/WOAH於4/17針對H5流感病毒發表風險評估,目前H5 2.3.4.4b病毒仍屬禽類病毒,人類病例多曾直/間接接觸易感動物,且未發生人際傳播能力,基於病毒廣泛存在於野生及飼養動物中,預期仍會持續出現病例,評估全球公共衛生風險仍低;感染風險部分,於一般大眾仍低,於常接觸受汙染動物或環境者則為低至中,主要因素為接觸的方式、時間、防護及管控措施等,呼籲各國加強對易感染動物及高危險人群之監測。
xNRhRjNCey2mVi-QYvNWmg.en: Summary for this week: Human cases: this week Viet Nam reported 1 new H5N1 human infection, and China reported 3 H9N2 human infections. Animal and poultry outbreaks (WAHIS): a total of 8 countries reported 33 new H5N1 outbreaks between 3 February and 17 April 2025: Hungary 11, Germany and the United Kingdom 7 each, the Netherlands 3, the United States 2, and one each in Romania, Estonia and Liberia. Japan reported 3 new H3N8 outbreaks on 10 April 2025. Avian influenza in US dairy cattle: Herds: since March last year, 1,021 (14) outbreaks have been reported cumulatively across 17 states, with recent cases concentrated in Idaho, California, Nevada and Arizona. Human infection via cattle: at least 9,300 cases have been monitored cumulatively, 218 tested, of which 41 were positive (conjunctivitis, respiratory and influenza-like symptoms). Other derived outbreaks: infections in domestic cats, sheep, alpacas and others, including a cat death. Wastewater surveillance: in week 15, 351 sampling sites provided test reports, and 3 sampling sites in 3 states (California, Iowa and New Jersey) detected H5-positive results. Other updates: on 18 April, Viet Nam reported one human H5N1 influenza infection in an 8-year-old girl from Biên Cầu District, Tây Ninh Province, in southeastern Viet Nam. The patient had a history of congenital heart disease. She developed fever, headache and vomiting from 11 April and was hospitalized; as her condition did not improve, she was transferred on 13 April. She later developed drowsiness, neck stiffness and altered consciousness, and was diagnosed with meningoencephalitis. H5 influenza was detected in her cerebrospinal fluid on 17 April, and H5N1 influenza was confirmed on 18 April; however, all her respiratory specimens were negative. She is still receiving treatment in the ICU, and her vital signs are temporarily stable. Investigation shows that she had contact with dead poultry two weeks before onset, and the investigation is ongoing. Experts say that detection of H5N1 influenza only in cerebrospinal fluid, with negative respiratory specimens, is a rare event; the country reported two children with similar symptoms in 2004, both of whom were severely ill and died. WHO updated information on a human H5N1 infection in Mexico: the patient was a 3-year-old girl from Durango State in the northwest, who developed fever and vomiting on 7 March, was hospitalized for respiratory failure on 13 March, received antiviral treatment, was confirmed on 1 April, and died of respiratory complications on 8 April. The virus was genotype D1.1 (belonging to the 2.3.4.4b clade), a genotype also detected in the United States and Canada, which have reported 5 human infection cases, one of them fatal. Contact investigations are all negative; the state has had no recent poultry outbreaks, but 3 other avian influenza outbreaks have been reported there this year. Annual summary: Human cases: 10 H5N1 influenza cases (973* cumulative since 2003) and 3 H9N2 influenza cases (131 cumulative); most cases had prior exposure to susceptible animals. (Following WHO counting methods, US H5 influenza cases are classified as H5N1 influenza cases.) Avian and animal cases: 1,557 highly and low pathogenic avian influenza outbreaks have been reported cumulatively by 50 countries and regions. Assessment and recommendations: FAO, WHO and WOAH published a risk assessment on H5 influenza viruses on 17 April. Currently, H5 2.3.4.4b viruses are still avian viruses; most human cases had direct or indirect contact with susceptible animals, and no human-to-human transmission has occurred. Because the virus is widespread in wild and farmed animals, cases are expected to continue, and the global public health risk is assessed as low. For infection risk, the risk is low for the general public and low to moderate for people who frequently contact contaminated animals or environments; the main factors are the mode and duration of contact, protective measures and control measures. Countries are urged to strengthen surveillance of susceptible animals and high-risk groups.

TjDG5pVbLGTYFsLzGS5OQw.zh: WHO於3/6召開小兒麻痺症第41次IHR會議,決議延長PHEIC至少3個月,針對各型病毒現況摘要如下:  WPV1:於阿富汗南部及巴基斯坦部分地區持續傳播,受影響範圍擴大,兩國疫苗覆蓋率不佳且疫苗接種計畫推動受阻,以及跨境交流頻繁,WPV1國際傳播風險持續。 cVDPV:國際傳播風險仍高,奈及利亞cVDPV2疫情嚴峻,非洲東北部衣索比亞疫情加劇,因人道及健康危機,使疫苗接種計畫無法順利推動,致當地未接種疫苗孩童大幅增加,葉門北部有眾多未接種疫苗之兒童,當地檢體運送亦受阻。另自2016年OPV2口服疫苗退場後,使各地區兒童免疫覆蓋率差距擴大。 cVDPV1病例數持續下降,惟剛果民主共和國於2024年出現新病例,顯示仍有免疫缺口。 cVDPV3超過2年無新增病例後,近期於法屬圭亞那及幾內亞報告環境樣本及新病例。
TjDG5pVbLGTYFsLzGS5OQw.en: WHO convened the 41st IHR Emergency Committee on poliomyelitis on 6 March and decided to extend the polio PHEIC by at least three months. A summary of the situation for each virus type is as follows. WPV1: continues to spread in southern Afghanistan and parts of Pakistan, with affected areas expanding. Poor vaccination coverage in both countries, obstacles to the vaccination programme and frequent cross-border movement mean the international transmission risk of WPV1 persists. cVDPV: the international transmission risk remains high. The cVDPV2 outbreak in Nigeria is severe, and the outbreak in Ethiopia in northeastern Africa has intensified; because of humanitarian and health crises, vaccination campaigns cannot proceed smoothly, and the number of unvaccinated children in the area has increased substantially. Northern Yemen has many unvaccinated children, and transport of local specimens has also been obstructed. In addition, since the withdrawal of the OPV2 oral vaccine in 2016, the gap in child immunity coverage between regions has widened. Cases of cVDPV1 continue to decline, but the Democratic Republic of the Congo reported new cases in 2024, indicating that immunity gaps remain. After more than two years without new cases, cVDPV3 has recently been reported in environmental samples and new cases in French Guiana and Guinea.

4Bf6VJ7h3hLVB49y7D4o9g.en: Epidemiological update: in week 10 of 2025 (3–9 March), global test positivity was about 3.1%, highest in the Americas region (3.6%), the European region (3.1%) and the African region (2.7%). 7L2OCyCkq9NKvXkhONJe_A.en: Epidemiological update: in week 9 of 2025 (24 February–2 March), global test positivity was about 3.2%, highest in the Americas (3.7%), Europe (3.2%) and Africa (2.3%). 3zhI2S9IY11vvR05s7DKjQ.zh: WHO於3/13宣布坦尚亞疫情結束,最後1例確診者於1/28死亡後已經連續42日(2倍潛伏期)未新增報告病例。此波疫情於1/20爆發,截至3/12累計報告10例死亡病例,其中2例確診,餘8例於未確診前即死亡(CFR:100%),年齡中位數為30歲(1-75歲),多數病例(7)為女性,另完成272名接觸者追蹤管理且均未發病。目前疫情來源仍不清楚,雖宣布疫情結束,惟仍存在病毒再次出現風險,評估該國家傳播風險為中,區域和全球風險則為低。
3zhI2S9IY11vvR05s7DKjQ.en: WHO declared the end of the outbreak in Tanzania on 13 March. The last confirmed case died on 28 January, and no new cases have been reported for 42 consecutive days, twice the incubation period. The outbreak began on 20 January. As of 12 March, 10 deaths had been reported cumulatively: 2 confirmed cases, and 8 people who died before being confirmed (CFR: 100%). The median age was 30 years (range 1–75). Most cases (7) were women. 272 contacts were traced and monitored, and none developed illness. The source of the outbreak remains unclear. Although the outbreak has been declared over, there remains a risk of the virus reappearing. WHO assesses the transmission risk in the country as moderate and the regional and global risk as low.

uU4XCJQWMlGr8JLE3OxB_g.zh: WHO公布於2025年2月25日召開M痘疫情IHR第三次緊急會議結論報告,表示目前疫情仍嚴峻,剛果民主共和國(DRC)等國疫情規模仍不明確,且國際間報告Ib分支感染國家數倍增,又因資金援助刪減,影響疫苗及診斷資源可近性,故宣布此波疫情持續構成「國際關注公共衛生緊急事件(PHEIC)」。 另針對各分支風險評估如下:  Ia分支:於DRC傳播風險為中; Ib分支:於DRC及鄰近區域傳播風險為高; II分支:於奈及利亞及中、西非區域傳播風險為中; IIb分支 : 國際傳播風險為中。
uU4XCJQWMlGr8JLE3OxB_g.en: WHO has published the conclusions of the third IHR Emergency Committee meeting on the mpox outbreak, held on 25 February 2025. It said the outbreak remains serious, the scale of outbreaks in countries such as the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) is still unclear, and the number of countries reporting clade Ib infections has multiplied. Reduced funding has affected access to vaccines and diagnostic resources. The Committee therefore declared that the outbreak continues to constitute a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC). Risk assessments by clade: clade Ia transmission risk in the DRC is moderate; clade Ib transmission risk in the DRC and neighbouring areas is high; clade II transmission risk in Nigeria and across central and west Africa is moderate; clade IIb international transmission risk is moderate.

rxH9xul0gEVJqUuF8sHqYA.zh: 本週摘要: 人類疫情:本週無人類感染病例。 禽/動物疫情(WAHIS):  共14國於2025/2/5~2025/3/13間新增84起H5N1疫情,美國19起、比利時14起、波蘭11起、荷蘭8起、匈牙利7起、德國/法國各5起、臺灣4起、羅馬亞/瑞典/柬埔寨/加拿大/丹麥各2起、芬蘭1起。 冰島於2025/2/3新增1起H5N5疫情。 烏克蘭於2025/3/7新增1起H5(N untyped)疫情。  美國乳牛感染禽流感案:  乳牛場:去年3月迄今累計17州報告985(7)起疫情,近期主要集中於加州、內華達州、亞利桑那州、愛達荷州。 人類經牛感染:累計監測至少9,000例,檢測217例,其中41例陽性(結膜炎、呼吸道及流感症狀)。 其他衍生疫情:感染家貓/羊/羊駝等,其中貓隻出現死亡案例。 廢水監測:第10週計467個採檢點提供檢測報告,9州29個採檢點檢出H5陽性。  其他更新:  比利時聯邦食品鏈安全局(AFSCA)於3/4公布該國西部東法蘭德斯省(East Flanders)一間禽場飼養之家貓檢出H5禽流感病毒,為該國首次於貓隻檢出,該禽場於2月曾爆發禽流感疫情。ECDC評估對一般民眾風險為低,對於職業暴露或接觸受禽流感感染之動物或受汙染之環境者,風險為低至中,目前尚無貓隻間或貓傳人之證據。 美國CDC研究評估H5N1病毒對抗病毒藥物的敏感性,研究樣本分別為2.3.2.1c分支(柬埔寨樣本)及2.3.4.4b(美洲樣本),結果顯示所有病毒對於常見之抗病毒藥物均有敏感性,惟效果各有差異;另除部分柬埔寨樣本外,其餘病毒於細胞培養測試中對治療A型流感的M2離子通道阻斷劑均呈現敏感性。  年度摘要  人類病例: 6例H5N1流感 (2003年迄今累計9691例),個案發病前多有易感動物相關暴露史。1依WHO統計方式將美國H5流感病例列為H5N1流感病例。 禽類/動物案例:累計46國家/地區通報1,086起高/低病原性禽流感疫情。  評估與建議: FAO/WHO/WOAH 12/20針對H5流感病毒發表風險評估,目前H5 2.3.4.4b病毒仍屬禽類病毒,人類病例多曾直/間接接觸易感動物,且未發生人際傳播能力,基於病毒廣泛存在於野生及飼養動物中,預期仍會持續出現病例,評估全球公共衛生風險仍低;感染風險部分,於一般大眾仍低,於常接觸受汙染動物或環境者則為低至中,主要取決於接觸的方式、時間、防護及管控措施等,呼籲各國加強對易感動物及高危險人群之監測。
rxH9xul0gEVJqUuF8sHqYA.en: Weekly summary. Human cases: no human infections were reported this week. Animal outbreaks (WAHIS): 14 countries reported 84 new H5N1 outbreaks between 5 February and 13 March 2025: the USA 19, Belgium 14, Poland 11, the Netherlands 8, Hungary 7, Germany and France 5 each, Taiwan 4, Romania, Sweden, Cambodia, Canada and Denmark 2 each, and Finland 1. Iceland reported one new H5N5 outbreak on 3 February 2025. Ukraine reported one new H5 (N untyped) outbreak on 7 March 2025. US dairy cattle avian influenza: dairy farms have reported 985 outbreaks cumulatively (7 new) in 17 states since March last year, recently concentrated in California, Nevada, Arizona and Idaho. Human infections linked to cattle: at least 9,000 people monitored cumulatively, 217 tested, and 41 positive (conjunctivitis, respiratory and influenza-like symptoms). Other spillover: infections in domestic cats, sheep, alpacas and others, with cat deaths. Wastewater surveillance: in week 10, 467 sampling sites reported results, with H5-positive detections at 29 sites in 9 states. Other updates: Belgium's Federal Agency for the Safety of the Food Chain (AFSCA) announced on 4 March that a domestic cat kept on a poultry farm in East Flanders, western Belgium, had tested positive for H5 avian influenza virus. This is the first detection in cats in Belgium; the farm had an avian influenza outbreak in February. ECDC assesses the risk to the general public as low, and the risk for occupational exposure or contact with infected animals or contaminated environments as low to moderate. There is currently no evidence of cat-to-cat or cat-to-human transmission. A US CDC study assessed the susceptibility of H5N1 viruses to antiviral drugs, using samples from clade 2.3.2.1c (Cambodian samples) and clade 2.3.4.4b (American samples). All viruses were sensitive to common antiviral drugs, although effects varied. Apart from some Cambodian samples, the other viruses were sensitive in cell culture tests to M2 ion channel blockers used to treat influenza A. Annual summary: 6 human H5N1 cases (9,691 cumulative since 2003), most with prior exposure to susceptible animals before onset. (Note: following WHO counting methods, US H5 influenza cases are classified as H5N1 cases.) Avian and animal cases: 46 countries and territories have reported 1,086 highly and low pathogenic avian influenza outbreaks cumulatively. Assessment and recommendations: FAO, WHO and WOAH published a risk assessment on H5 influenza viruses on 20 December. H5 2.3.4.4b viruses are still avian viruses; human cases have generally involved direct or indirect contact with susceptible animals, and there is no human-to-human transmission capacity. Because the virus is widespread in wild and domestic animals, cases are expected to continue, and the global public health risk is assessed as low. The risk is low for the general public, and low to moderate for people who often handle contaminated animals or environments, depending mainly on the type and duration of exposure, protection and control measures. Countries are urged to strengthen surveillance of susceptible animals and high-risk groups.

swJGMI4UQt9Qk3py5BAniw.en: Epidemiological update: in week 8 of 2025 (17–23 February), global test positivity was about 3.5%, highest in the Americas (4.1%), Europe (3.5%) and Africa (3.2%). QvE6w8eAzXgQV-drBmEISg.zh: 本週摘要 人類疫情:本週無人類感染病例。 禽/動物疫情(WAHIS):  共20國於2024/12/13~2025/3/6間新增91起H5N1疫情,分別為英國29起、美國16起、德國12起、匈牙利10起、荷蘭5起、瑞典3起、柬埔寨/波蘭各2起、羅馬亞/墨西哥/摩爾多瓦/愛爾蘭/挪威/俄羅斯/阿爾巴亞/法國/希臘/西班牙/比利時/丹麥各1起。 英國於2025/2/17新增1起H5N5疫情。 比利時於2025/1/5-2/27間新增2起H5(N untyped)疫情。  美國乳牛感染禽流感案  乳牛場:去年3月迄今累計17州報告978(2)起疫情,近期主要集中於加州、內華達州、亞利桑那州、愛達荷州。 人類經牛感染:累計監測至少8,900例,檢測217例,其中41例陽性(結膜炎、呼吸道及流感症狀)。 其他衍生疫情:感染家貓/羊/羊駝等,其中貓隻出現死亡案例。 廢水監測:第9週計453個採檢點提供檢測報告,4州8個採檢點檢出H5陽性。  其他更新  美國CDC公布H5N1流感對該國民眾風險評估:尚無證據顯示病毒於該國具人際傳播能力,且多數報告病例多具有受感染動物接觸史,評估一般民眾感染風險為低;倘接觸受感染動物或受汙染之物品或液體,其風險為中至高,該評估具中等信心水準。風險評估仍可能改變,因A型流感可迅速突變,具引發全球大流行之潛在可能性。H5N1流感病毒已於人類密切接觸動物中高度流行,增加突變及基因重組機會,且季節性A流與H5N1病毒同時感染同一人類或動物,可能產生兼具兩者病毒特徵之新型流感病毒,該病毒可能更易於人際傳播。已開發H5流感候選疫苗,預期可有效對抗目前於野鳥、家禽及牛隻間流行病毒,倘有需要亦能用於生產人用疫苗。 中國發布禽源性H3N2犬流感病毒(CIV)研究報告,研究團隊於2023年12月至2024年2月間蒐集131件具呼吸道症狀之貓狗拭子樣本,於此批樣本中分離出一流感病毒株,發現具人類流感病毒相的氨基酸替換,其研究結果顯示H3N2 CIV (canine influenza virus)朝向適應哺乳動物宿主之方向演化,有對其加強監測及風險評估之必要性。  年度摘要:  人類病例: 6例H5N1流感 (2003年迄今累計9691例),個案發病前多有易感動物相關暴露史。1本週依WHO統計方式將美國H5流感病例列為H5N1流感病例。 禽類/動物案例:累計46國家/地區通報1,000起高/低病原性禽流感疫情。  評估與建議: FAO/WHO/WOAH 12/20針對H5流感病毒發表風險評估,目前H5 2.3.4.4b病毒仍屬禽類病毒,人類病例多曾直/間接接觸易感動物,且未發生人際傳播能力,基於病毒廣泛存在於野生及飼養動物中,預期仍會持續出現病例,評估全球公共衛生風險仍低;感染風險部分,於一般大眾仍低,於常接觸受汙染動物或環境者則為低至中,主要取決於接觸的方式、時間、防護及管控措施等,呼籲各國加強對易感動物及高危險人群之監測。
QvE6w8eAzXgQV-drBmEISg.en: Weekly summary. Human cases: no human infections were reported this week. Animal outbreaks (WAHIS): 20 countries reported 91 new H5N1 outbreaks between 13 December 2024 and 6 March 2025: the UK 29, the USA 16, Germany 12, Hungary 10, the Netherlands 5, Sweden 3, Cambodia and Poland 2 each, and Romania, Mexico, Moldova, Ireland, Norway, Russia, Albania, France, Greece, Spain, Belgium and Denmark 1 each. The UK reported one new H5N5 outbreak on 17 February 2025. Belgium reported two new H5 (N untyped) outbreaks between 5 January and 27 February 2025. US dairy cattle avian influenza: dairy farms have reported 978 outbreaks cumulatively (2 new) in 17 states since March last year, recently concentrated in California, Nevada, Arizona and Idaho. Human infections linked to cattle: at least 8,900 people monitored cumulatively, 217 tested, and 41 positive (conjunctivitis, respiratory and influenza-like symptoms). Other spillover: infections in domestic cats, sheep, alpacas and others, with cat deaths. Wastewater surveillance: in week 9, 453 sampling sites reported results, with H5-positive detections at 8 sites in 4 states. Other updates: the US CDC has published its risk assessment of H5N1 influenza for the US public. There is no evidence so far that the virus can spread between people in the United States, and most reported cases had contact with infected animals. The risk to the general public is assessed as low; for people exposed to infected animals or to contaminated objects or fluids, the risk is assessed as moderate to high. This assessment has moderate confidence. The assessment may change, because influenza A viruses can mutate rapidly and have the potential to cause a global pandemic. H5N1 is highly prevalent among animals in close contact with humans, which increases opportunities for mutation and reassortment. If seasonal influenza A and H5N1 infect the same person or animal, a novel influenza virus with characteristics of both could emerge, which might spread more easily between people. H5 influenza candidate vaccines have been developed and are expected to be effective against viruses currently circulating among wild birds, poultry and cattle, and could be used to produce human vaccines if needed. China has published a study on avian-origin H3N2 canine influenza virus (CIV). Between December 2023 and February 2024, the research team collected 131 respiratory swab samples from cats and dogs with respiratory symptoms, and isolated one influenza virus strain from these samples. The strain showed amino acid substitutions resembling those of human influenza viruses. The results suggest that H3N2 CIV is evolving toward adaptation to mammalian hosts, so enhanced surveillance and risk assessment are needed. Annual summary: 6 human H5N1 cases (9,691 cumulative since 2003), most with prior exposure to susceptible animals before onset. This week, following WHO counting methods, US H5 influenza cases are classified as H5N1 cases. Avian and animal cases: 46 countries and territories have reported 1,000 highly and low pathogenic avian influenza outbreaks cumulatively. Assessment and recommendations: FAO, WHO and WOAH published a risk assessment on H5 influenza viruses on 20 December. H5 2.3.4.4b viruses are still avian viruses; human cases have generally involved direct or indirect contact with susceptible animals, and there is no human-to-human transmission capacity. Because the virus is widespread in wild and domestic animals, cases are expected to continue, and the global public health risk is assessed as low. The risk is low for the general public, and low to moderate for people who often handle contaminated animals or environments, depending mainly on the type and duration of exposure, protection and control measures. Countries are urged to strengthen surveillance of susceptible animals and high-risk groups.

padTMb1Yv7r4pi9N3ScHww.en: Epidemiological update: in week 7 of 2025 (10–16 February), global test positivity was about 3.8%, highest in the Americas (4.9%), Europe (3.7%) and Africa (2.4%). Japan's cases continue to decline: in week 9 (24 February–2 March), sentinel clinic reports exceeded 21,700, an average of 4.42 cases per sentinel clinic. Brazil reported over 9,100 cases in week 7 (10–16 February); about 132 deaths were reported in the past month (17 January–16 February). Severe cases were mainly among children and older people, and deaths were mainly among older people. Assessment and recommendations: global test positivity is declining, with recent declines in all regional offices. The main global variant is XEC, and the share of LP.8.1 is also rising. WHO notes that most countries now include COVID-19 in routine respiratory infection surveillance, and recommends that countries provide affordable and reliable testing, treatment and vaccines, maintain early warning and surveillance systems, continue tracking variant trends, report epidemic information to WHO, and maintain the infrastructure established during the COVID-19 period.

F6B6v6w2VWHI6ickjrVE6g.zh: WHO於2/20公布2025年第1-4週累計3區署共19國家/地區34,000餘例病例,其中349例死亡,分別相較去年12月下降27%與33%,疫情趨緩可能與冬季傳播下降相關,病例數以非洲、東地中海區及東南亞區為多。WHO評估全球疫情風險仍為非常高。 非洲2025年截至2/21(第8週)累計10國/地區2,6000餘例、其中616死亡(CFR:22.8%),疫情持續擴大,病例數累計前五名分別為南蘇丹(12,711)、蘇丹(5,063)、安哥拉(4,914)、迦納(2,152)、衣索比亞(857)。
F6B6v6w2VWHI6ickjrVE6g.en: On 20 February WHO reported that, in weeks 1–4 of 2025, 19 countries and territories across 3 WHO regions had reported a cumulative total of over 34,000 cases, of which 349 died. Compared with December last year, these were down 27% for cases and 33% for deaths. The slowdown may be related to reduced winter transmission. Cases were concentrated in the African, Eastern Mediterranean and South-East Asia regions. WHO assesses the global risk as still very high. In Africa, from the start of 2025 to 21 February (week 8), 10 countries and territories have reported over 26,000 cases cumulatively, including 616 deaths (CFR: 22.8%). The outbreak continues to expand. The top five countries by cumulative cases are South Sudan (12,711), Sudan (5,063), Angola (4,914), Ghana (2,152) and Ethiopia (857).

0mNNmuyFGyQwGL7fuiH1Iw.zh: WHO公布其諮詢委員會針對2025-26年北半球流感季之疫苗病毒株建議,其中H3N2病毒株更換,H1N1與B型流感病毒株則保留,另H3N2對於雞胚蛋培養與細胞培養分別提供不同病毒株建議。 WHO更新人畜共通流感病毒株審查,新增2種禽流感病毒株為新候選疫苗株,分別為H5N1(2.3.2.1a)分支及H5N6(2.3.4.4h)分支,2.3.2.1a分支於南亞禽鳥及貓科動物檢出,而2.3.4.4h分支曾於東南亞流行,近期於中國東南省分重新出現,於2024年報告2例人類感染。
0mNNmuyFGyQwGL7fuiH1Iw.en: WHO published its advisory committee's recommendations on vaccine virus strains for the 2025–26 northern hemisphere influenza season. The H3N2 strain is to be replaced, while the H1N1 and B strains are retained. For H3N2, the recommendations differ for egg-based and cell-based culture. WHO also updated its review of zoonotic influenza viruses, adding two avian influenza strains as new candidate vaccine viruses: clade H5N1 (2.3.2.1a) and clade H5N6 (2.3.4.4h). Clade 2.3.2.1a has been detected in birds and felids in South Asia. Clade 2.3.4.4h circulated in Southeast Asia and has recently re-emerged in provinces of southeastern China, with 2 human infections reported in 2024.

wZHvAQOC0v5w8Hdv3CL0qw.zh: 本月更新:  自2022年5月截至今年2/28全球累計131國/地區報告12萬8,627例確診病例,其中至少287例死亡(CFR:0.2%)。 今年截至第9週全球累計63國/地區報告7,915例確診病例,其中非洲區6,047例、西太平洋區757例、美洲區665例、歐洲區425例、東南亞區13例及東地中海區8例。  其他更新:  南非於2/25新增1例Ib型確診病例,病患為成年男性,具烏干達旅遊史。 德國於2/21新增1例Ib型確診病例,病患為成年男性,旅遊史未明。  評估與建議: WHO於2/25召開針對2024年M痘疫情的IHR緊急委員會第三次會議,基於「病例數繼續上升、地理傳播持續存在、剛果民主共和國東部暴力阻礙反應,以及缺乏資金貫徹因應計畫」等,宣告此波疫情仍然構成「國際關注公共衛生緊急事件(PHEIC)」,並發布效期至今年8/20之臨時建議措施,包括緊急協調、監控與防控及疫苗接種等8項措施,並請各國須定期向WHO報告臨時建議的執行情況。
wZHvAQOC0v5w8Hdv3CL0qw.en: Monthly update: since May 2022 and as of 28 February 2025, 131 countries and territories have cumulatively reported 128,627 confirmed cases globally, including at least 287 deaths (CFR: 0.2%). As of week 9 this year, 63 countries and territories have reported 7,915 confirmed cases in total: African Region 6,047, Western Pacific Region 757, Region of the Americas 665, European Region 425, South-East Asia Region 13 and Eastern Mediterranean Region 8. Other updates: South Africa reported one new clade Ib confirmed case on 25 February; the patient is an adult man with a travel history to Uganda. Germany reported one new clade Ib confirmed case on 21 February; the patient is an adult man, and travel history is unknown. Assessment and recommendations: WHO held the third meeting of the IHR Emergency Committee on the 2024 mpox outbreak on 25 February. Citing continuing increases in cases, persistent geographic spread, violence in eastern DRC impeding the response, and a lack of funding to implement response plans, it declared that the outbreak continues to constitute a PHEIC. Temporary recommendations, valid until 20 August this year, were issued. They comprise eight measures, including emergency coordination, surveillance and control, and vaccination, and countries are asked to report regularly to WHO on implementation.

ueXJuyBrsYjgctMngqQTkA.en: Epidemiological update: in week 6 of 2025 (3–9 February), global test positivity was about 4.3%, highest in the African region (6.9%), the Americas (5.2%) and Europe (4.3%). AR6F8HMgY13OOg9cBIm_4w.en: Weekly summary. Human cases: the USA reported one new human H5N1 infection this week. Animal outbreaks (WAHIS): 21 countries reported 175 new H5N1 outbreaks between 1 February 2024 and 18 February 2025: the UK 62, the USA 28, the Philippines 25, Taiwan 13, Germany 11, Poland and Hungary 6 each, Belgium 4, Switzerland, Nigeria and India 3 each, Greece 2, and Ireland, Austria, Cambodia, Bulgaria, Finland, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Nepal, Japan and Türkiye 1 each. Australia reported one new H7N8 outbreak on 17 February 2025. Argentina reported one new H5 (N untyped) outbreak on 11 February 2025. US dairy cattle avian influenza: dairy farms have reported 973 outbreaks cumulatively (5 new) in 17 states since March last year, recently concentrated in California, Nevada and Arizona. Human infections linked to cattle: at least 8,900 people monitored cumulatively, 217 tested, and 41 positive (conjunctivitis, respiratory and influenza-like symptoms). Other spillover: infections in domestic cats, sheep, alpacas and others, with cat deaths. Wastewater surveillance: in week 7, 360 sampling sites reported results, with H5-positive detections at 12 sites in 3 states. Other updates: Arizona in the USA reported detecting H5N1 in cow's milk, genotype D1.1. The USDA said this genotype was a common main type among wild migratory birds last autumn and winter, and has been found in wild birds and mammals. Genetic testing shows this case was an independent event in which wild birds transmitted HPAI to dairy cattle; it is the third detection of HPAI spillover into cattle. Current evidence suggests that the risk of HPAI entering dairy farms via wild birds is rising. In addition, the US CDC on 20 February published a report of a suspected human-to-cat H5N1 transmission: H5N1 was detected in cats at the homes of 2 dairy farm workers. The cats had not been in contact with infected farms. The 2 workers declined testing, and other contacts tested negative. The Public Health Agency of Canada announced on 19 February that it will purchase 500,000 doses of human avian influenza vaccine, using the H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b as the antigen, as part of an emergency plan. The vaccine will be used for populations at risk of exposure to infected animals. Canada reported its first human H5N1 case on 9 November last year. Avian and animal cases: 40 countries have reported 669 highly and low pathogenic avian influenza outbreaks cumulatively. The risk is low for the general public, and low to moderate for people who often handle contaminated animals or environments, depending mainly on the type and duration of exposure, protection and control measures. Countries are urged to strengthen surveillance of susceptible animals and high-risk groups.

jBRX6YJKF09Wbb2uyYQ4_Q.en: Epidemiological update: in week 5 of 2025 (27 January–2 February), global test positivity was about 4.0%, highest in the Americas (5.6%), Africa (4.9%) and Europe (3.9%). Japan's cases have declined recently; in week 7 of 2025 (10–16 February), sentinel clinic reports exceeded 25,000, an average of 5.15 per sentinel clinic. WHO global update: over the 28 days from 9 December 2024 to 5 January 2025, more than 160,000 cases and 3,300 deaths were newly reported globally. lGkL302hkyJAvUfCxMV-Pw.en: Portugal's Madeira Islands reported 2 locally acquired cases in early February. Authorities said that since symptoms began in January, the cases have passed their infectious period, and they assess the outbreak as under control. Prevention and control measures have been strengthened. The region had an outbreak in 2012–2013 that reported over 1,000 cases.

KcqdQvDCS4hTvfDOvAbKQA.zh: 本週摘要:  人類疫情:美國於本週新增1例H5N1人類感染病例。  禽/動物疫情(WAHIS):  共16國於2024/1/20~2025/2/11間新增192起H5N1疫情,分別為日本47起、荷蘭44起、英國23起、德國20起、美國18起、波蘭8起、義大利/韓國/印度各6起、比利時5起、奈及利亞3起、摩爾多瓦2起、烏克蘭/波士亞/匈牙利/日各1起。 加拿大於2025/1/15新增1起H5N5疫情。 澳大利亞於2025/2/3~2025/2/10間新增2起H7N8疫情。  美國乳牛感染禽流感案:  乳牛場:去年3月迄今累計16州報告968(9)起疫情,近期主要集中於加州、內華達州。 人類經牛感染:累計監測至少8,700例,檢測194例,其中41例陽性(結膜炎、呼吸道及流感症狀)。 其他衍生疫情:感染家貓/羊/羊駝等,其中貓隻出現死亡案例。 廢水監測:第6週計387個採檢點提供檢測報告,3州15個採檢點檢出H5陽性。  其他更新:  美國新增2例疑H5N1人類感染病例,首例為俄亥俄州默瑟郡(Mercer County)農場工人,曾接觸死禽,其他流行病學資訊未提供;案2為懷俄明州普拉特郡(Platte County)女性長者,具有其他潛在疾病,目前重症住院,另病患家中後院飼養雞隻生病後死亡,兩案皆為該州首例疑病例,仍待CDC公布確診資訊。 美國CDC於2/13發布調查報告,針對2024年乳牛感染H5N1疫情期間,來自美國及加拿大150名獸醫進行血清流行病學調查,發現3名無症狀感染者體內存在HPAI A(H5)抗體,報告指出感染者中有2名表示未接觸過受HPAI感染動物,1名於尚未報告乳牛感染疫情地區執業,顯示該國可能有H5流感之人及動物感染者尚未被發現;另感染者於照顧牛隻時並未佩戴口罩及護目鏡,顯示病毒可透過呼吸道、部及腸胃道暴露造成感染,報告建議加強牛群及散裝牛奶檢測,以監測更多H5流感陽性牛群,提高對畜牧從業人員保護。  年度摘要:  人類病例: 3例H5N1流感 (2003年迄今累計911例),個案發病前多有易感動物相關暴露史。 禽類/動物案例:累計35國報告585起高/低病原性禽流感疫情。  評估與建議: FAO/WHO/WOAH 12/20針對H5流感病毒發表風險評估,目前H5 2.3.4.4b病毒仍屬禽類病毒,人類病例多曾直/間接接觸易感動物,且未發生人際傳播能力,基於病毒廣泛存在於野生及飼養動物中,預期仍會持續出現病例,評估全球公共衛生風險仍低;感染風險部分,於一般大眾仍低,於常接觸受汙染動物或環境者則為低至中,主要取決於接觸的方式、時間、防護及管控措施等,呼籲各國加強對易感動物及高危險人群之監測。
KcqdQvDCS4hTvfDOvAbKQA.en: Weekly summary. Human cases: the USA reported one new human H5N1 infection this week. Animal outbreaks (WAHIS): 16 countries reported 192 new H5N1 outbreaks between 20 January 2024 and 11 February 2025: Japan 47, the Netherlands 44, the UK 23, Germany 20, the USA 18, Poland 8, Italy, South Korea and India 6 each, Belgium 5, Nigeria 3, Moldova 2, and Ukraine, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Hungary and Japan 1 each. Canada reported one new H5N5 outbreak on 15 January 2025. Australia reported 2 new H7N8 outbreaks between 3 and 10 February 2025. US dairy cattle avian influenza: dairy farms have reported 968 outbreaks cumulatively (9 new) in 16 states since March last year, recently concentrated in California and Nevada. Human infections linked to cattle: at least 8,700 people monitored cumulatively, 194 tested, and 41 positive (conjunctivitis, respiratory and influenza-like symptoms). Other spillover: infections in domestic cats, sheep, alpacas and others, with cat deaths. Wastewater surveillance: in week 6, 387 sampling sites reported results, with H5-positive detections at 15 sites in 3 states. Other updates: the USA reported 2 new suspected human H5N1 infections. The first was a farm worker in Mercer County, Ohio, who had been exposed to dead poultry; no other epidemiological information was provided. Case 2 is an elderly woman in Platte County, Wyoming, with underlying conditions, currently hospitalized in serious condition; backyard chickens at her home fell ill and died. Both cases are the first suspected cases in their states, and CDC confirmation is pending. On 13 February the US CDC published an investigation report. Serological surveys of 150 veterinarians from the USA and Canada during the 2024 H5N1 dairy cattle outbreak found HPAI A(H5) antibodies in 3 asymptomatic people. Two of them reported no exposure to infected animals, and one practised in an area where cattle infections had not yet been reported, suggesting that undetected human and animal H5 infections may exist in the country. The infected people did not wear masks or goggles when caring for cattle, which indicates the virus may infect through the respiratory tract, eyes and gastrointestinal tract. The report recommends strengthening testing of herds and bulk milk to detect more H5-positive herds and better protect livestock workers. Annual summary: 3 human H5N1 cases (911 cumulative since 2003), most with prior exposure to susceptible animals before onset. Avian and animal cases: 35 countries have reported 585 highly and low pathogenic avian influenza outbreaks cumulatively. Assessment and recommendations: FAO, WHO and WOAH published a risk assessment on H5 influenza viruses on 20 December. H5 2.3.4.4b viruses are still avian viruses; human cases have generally involved direct or indirect contact with susceptible animals, and there is no human-to-human transmission capacity. Because the virus is widespread in wild and domestic animals, cases are expected to continue, and the global public health risk is assessed as low. The risk is low for the general public, and low to moderate for people who often handle contaminated animals or environments, depending mainly on the type and duration of exposure, protection and control measures. Countries are urged to strengthen surveillance of susceptible animals and high-risk groups.

PX9a20TewR6byDBqQo-HUQ.en: Epidemiological update: in week 4 of 2025 (20–26 January), global test positivity was about 5.0%, highest in the African region (7.3%), the Americas (6.2%) and Europe (5.0%). In Japan, case numbers have trended upward since mid-November 2024 and have recently fluctuated; in week 6 of 2025 (3–9 February), sentinel clinic reports exceeded 28,000, an average of 5.82 per sentinel clinic. Mainland China's January situation: 33,218 confirmed cases were added, with case numbers fluctuating and trending downward. There were 163 severe cases and 4 deaths. Compared with December (112 severe cases and 7 deaths), severe cases rose while deaths fell slightly. Test positivity was at a low point, with XDV and JN.1 and their descendant variants the main circulating strains. In Hong Kong SAR, test positivity and the outpatient consultation rate were at a low point in week 6; the LP.8.1 variant was detected in wastewater surveillance, and JN.1 and its descendants remain the main circulating strains. Assessment and recommendations: according to WHO data, global test positivity has recently been declining. In early January (6–12 January), the XEC variant accounted for the highest share globally and was rising, followed by KP.3.1.1, whose share was falling. WHO notes that most countries now include COVID-19 in routine respiratory infection surveillance, and recommends that countries provide affordable and reliable testing, treatment and vaccines, maintain early warning and surveillance systems, continue tracking variant trends, report epidemic information to WHO, and maintain the infrastructure established during the COVID-19 period.

FeSz4ZO5vRp3iTgfnvNsCQ.zh: 疫情更新:  2025年第3週(1/13-1/19)全球陽性率約5.8%,陽性率以非洲區(12.0%)、美洲區(7.1%)及歐洲區(5.7%)為高。 美國近期陽性率呈下降趨勢,急診就診率亦下降且以幼童及老年人為多,以變異株XEC、KP.3.1.1及LP.8.1占比為高。 歐洲區陽性率呈下降趨勢,主要流行變異株為XEC;第3週英國、希臘及俄羅斯分別新增800-10,000餘例病例。 WHO於1/24將變異株LP.8.1列為監測中變異株(VUM),於全球占比上升,2024年第51週(12/16-12/22)至2025年第2週(1/6-1/12)變異株LP.8.1占比變化,於西太平洋區由0.8%上升至7.5%,於美洲區由2.2%上升至7.9%,於歐洲區由1.6%上升至2.5%,評估對全球公共衛生的風險為低。  評估與建議: 全球陽性率呈下降趨勢,其中,東地中海區上升,東南亞區上下波動,其他地區則下降。依據WHO資料顯示,於2025年1月上旬(1/6-1/12),全球流行變異株以XEC占比46.8%最高,呈上升趨勢,其次為變異株KP.3.1.1占比26.9%,呈下降趨勢。WHO表示多數國家已將COVID-19納入常規呼吸道傳染病監測,建議各國提供民眾可負擔及可信賴的檢測、治療及疫苗,維持預警監視系統及持續追蹤變異株趨勢,並向WHO通報疫情資訊及維繫COVID-19期間所建立之基礎設施。
FeSz4ZO5vRp3iTgfnvNsCQ.en: Epidemic update: In week 3 of 2025 (13–19 January), the global positivity rate was about 5.8%, highest in the African Region (12.0%), the Region of the Americas (7.1%) and the European Region (5.7%). In the United States, the recent positivity rate has declined, and emergency department visit rates have also fallen, mainly among young children and older adults; the predominant variants are XEC, KP.3.1.1 and LP.8.1. In the European Region, the positivity rate is declining, with XEC as the main circulating variant; in week 3, the United Kingdom, Greece and Russia each reported between 800 and just over 10,000 new cases. WHO designated variant LP.8.1 as a Variant Under Monitoring (VUM) on 24 January. Its share of global variants rose between week 51 of 2024 (16–22 December) and week 2 of 2025 (6–12 January): in the Western Pacific Region from 0.8% to 7.5%, in the Region of the Americas from 2.2% to 7.9%, and in the European Region from 1.6% to 2.5%. WHO assesses the risk to global public health as low. Assessment and recommendations: Global positivity is declining; it is rising in the Eastern Mediterranean Region, fluctuating in the South-East Asia Region, and declining elsewhere. According to WHO data, in early January 2025 (6–12 January), XEC was the leading global circulating variant at 46.8%, with an upward trend, followed by KP.3.1.1 at 26.9%, with a downward trend. WHO notes that most countries have integrated COVID-19 into routine respiratory infection surveillance, and recommends that countries provide affordable and reliable testing, treatment and vaccines, maintain early warning and surveillance systems, continue tracking variant trends, report epidemic information to WHO, and maintain the infrastructure established during the COVID-19 period.

zc3Ox9pWLtnMp7jfzKkTBQ.zh: 全球去年報告,WHO之5個區署累計共80萬餘例病例、5千8百餘例死亡。東地中海區(8國)佔比最多,累計59萬餘例、2千4百餘例死亡;其次為非洲區(18國),累計17萬餘例、3千1百餘例;東南亞區為1萬9千餘例病例、58例死亡,美洲區為1萬餘例病例、162例死亡。病例最多國家依序為葉門(26萬餘例)、阿富汗(17萬餘例)、巴基斯坦(7萬6千餘例)。死亡數國家依序為蘇丹(1,296例)、葉門(879例)、奈及利亞(726例)。 安哥拉疫情上升且嚴峻,自1/7-29累計6個省報告1,081例病例、45例死亡,首例發生於西部魯安達省,該省病例占7成(748例),病患年齡介於2-86歲,當局已於1/27開始疫苗接種活動。前一次爆發疫情為2018年,累計3省1,262例病例、19例死亡。
zc3Ox9pWLtnMp7jfzKkTBQ.en: Global reporting for last year: the five WHO regional offices together reported over 800,000 cases and over 5,800 deaths. The Eastern Mediterranean Region (8 countries) accounted for the largest share, with a cumulative 590,000+ cases and 2,400+ deaths; followed by the African Region (18 countries), with 170,000+ cases and 3,100+ deaths. The South-East Asia Region reported 19,000+ cases and 58 deaths, and the Region of the Americas reported 10,000+ cases and 162 deaths. The countries with the most cases were Yemen (260,000+), Afghanistan (170,000+) and Pakistan (76,000+). The countries with the most deaths were Sudan (1,296), Yemen (879) and Nigeria (726). Angola: the outbreak is increasing and severe. From 7 to 29 January, six provinces cumulatively reported 1,081 cases and 45 deaths. The first case occurred in Luanda Province in the west, which accounts for 70% of cases (748); patients are aged 2–86. Authorities began vaccination activities on 27 January. The previous outbreak, in 2018, reported 1,262 cases and 19 deaths in three provinces.

7tGr90gzUl0UHWSDye6PXw.zh: 本月更新:  自2022年5月截至今年01/31全球累計128國/地區報告12萬4,753例確診病例,其中至少272例死亡(CFR:0.2%)。 今年截至第5週全球累計42國/地區報告4,800例確診病例,其中非洲區3,846例、西太平洋區560例、美洲區210例、歐洲區178例、東南亞區5例及東地中海區1例。  其他更新:  英國於1/27-1/31間新增2例Ib型確診病例,個案近期皆自烏干達返國,該國自2024年10月以來確診病例數達8例(5例境外移入,3例本土感染);迄今共11個非非洲國家報告Ib分支輸入病例,包括瑞典/泰國/印度/德國/英國/美國/加拿大/巴基斯坦/比利時/中國/法國。 獅子山及亞塞拜然分別於1/10及1/18報告首例確診病例。  評估與建議: WHO於2024/8/14宣告此波疫情構成「國際關注公共衛生緊急事件(PHEIC)」,另於11/22針對各分支風險評估如下:  Ia分支:公衛風險為高,國內/國際傳播風險為高; Ib分支:公衛風險為高,國內/國際傳播風險為高; II分支:公衛風險為中,國內/國際傳播風險為中。
7tGr90gzUl0UHWSDye6PXw.en: This month's update: From May 2022 through 31 January this year, 128 countries and territories worldwide have cumulatively reported 124,753 confirmed cases, including at least 272 deaths (CFR 0.2%). So far this year, up to week 5, 42 countries and territories have reported 4,800 confirmed cases: 3,846 in the African Region, 560 in the Western Pacific Region, 210 in the Region of the Americas, 178 in the European Region, 5 in the South-East Asia Region and 1 in the Eastern Mediterranean Region. Other updates: The United Kingdom reported two new confirmed clade Ib cases between 27 and 31 January; both had recently returned from Uganda. Since October 2024 the country has recorded 8 confirmed cases (5 imported, 3 locally acquired). So far, 11 non-African countries have reported imported clade Ib cases, including Sweden, Thailand, India, Germany, the United Kingdom, the United States, Canada, Pakistan, Belgium, China and France. Sierra Leone and Azerbaijan reported their first confirmed cases on 10 and 18 January, respectively. Assessment and recommendations: WHO declared this mpox wave a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) on 14 August 2024, and on 22 November assessed the risks for each clade: clade Ia has high public health risk and high national and international transmission risk; clade Ib has high public health risk and high national and international transmission risk; clade II has moderate public health risk and moderate national and international transmission risk.

IDlM1ErBEOtMDoEjDvvLBA.zh: 本週摘要:  人類疫情:英國於本週新增1例H5N1人類感染病例。 禽/動物疫情(WAHIS):   共29國於2022/12/30~2025/1/30間新增328起H5N1疫情,分別為美國74起、智利53起、荷蘭29起、德國/英國各22起、義大利17起、波蘭16起、日本15起、韓國14起、匈牙利10起、奈及利亞/以色列各7起、奧地利6起、捷克5起、越南/法國/印度各4起、葡萄牙/加拿大各3起、墨西哥/愛爾蘭/立陶宛各2起、羅馬亞/摩爾多瓦/哥倫比亞/柬埔寨/芬蘭/比利時/丹麥各1起。 共2國於2024/10/14~2025/1/19間新增2起H5N5疫情,分別為挪威/冰島各1起。 共2國於2024/11/23~2025/1/2間新增5起H5(N untyped)疫情,分別為美國4起、祕魯1起。  美國乳牛感染禽流感案  乳牛場:去年3月迄今累計16州報告951(23)起疫情,近期主要集中於加州。 人類經牛感染:累計監測至少8,500例,檢測170例,其中40例陽性(結膜炎、呼吸道及流感症狀)。 其他衍生疫情:感染家貓/羊/羊駝等,其中貓隻出現死亡案例。 廢水監測:第4週計328個採檢點提供檢測報告,5州33個採檢點檢出H5陽性。  其他更新:  英國於1/28公布1例與農場大量病禽長期密切接觸之H5N1感染病例,為該國自2022年以來首例;患者來自中部西米德蘭茲地區,目前狀況良好,該農場病禽感染DI.2 基因型,為已知在該國鳥類中傳播之病毒,與美國哺乳動物和鳥類中傳播病毒株不同。迄未發現人與人間傳播情況,評估公眾感染風險仍然非常低。當局近期已將H5禽流感疫苗添加為國家儲備物資。 美國FDA更新寵物食品規範,以肉類、牛奶及雞蛋為原料且未經高溫加熱處理之寵物食品,需將高病原性禽流感(以H5N1為主)列入食品安全計畫,將其列為已知或可預見的危害,減少經生食感染寵物之風險;美國農業部於去年12月下旬發現火雞與家貓感染存在關聯,於今年1月更新監測政策,將加強火雞高病原性禽流感監測。 美國CDC因應季節性流感活動增加期間零星出現的人類感染新型A型流感H5N1病毒案例,建議縮短住院病患之A型流感樣本進行分型時間,以減少延遲鑑別診斷情形。  年度摘要:  人類病例: H5N1流感2例(2003年迄今累計910例),個案發病前多有易感動物相關暴露史。 禽類/動物案例:累計29國報告303起高/低病原性禽流感疫情。  評估與建議: FAO/WHO/WOAH 12/20針對H5流感病毒發表風險評估,目前H5 2.3.4.4b病毒仍屬禽類病毒,人類病例多曾直/間接接觸易感動物,且未發生人際傳播能力,基於病毒廣泛存在於野生及飼養動物中,預期仍會持續出現病例,評估全球公共衛生風險仍低;感染風險部分,於一般大眾仍低,於常接觸受汙染動物或環境者則為低至中,主要取決於接觸的方式、時間、防護及管控措施等,呼籲各國加強對易感動物及高危險人群之監測。
IDlM1ErBEOtMDoEjDvvLBA.en: Weekly summary. Human cases: The United Kingdom reported one new human H5N1 infection this week. Avian and animal outbreaks (WAHIS): 29 countries reported 328 new H5N1 outbreaks between 30 December 2022 and 30 January 2025: United States 74, Chile 53, Netherlands 29, Germany and United Kingdom 22 each, Italy 17, Poland 16, Japan 15, South Korea 14, Hungary 10, Nigeria and Israel 7 each, Austria 6, Czechia 5, Viet Nam, France and India 4 each, Portugal and Canada 3 each, Mexico, Ireland and Lithuania 2 each, and Romania, Moldova, Colombia, Cambodia, Finland, Belgium and Denmark 1 each. Between 14 October 2024 and 19 January 2025, 2 countries reported 2 new H5N5 outbreaks, one each in Norway and Iceland. Between 23 November 2024 and 2 January 2025, 2 countries reported 5 new H5 (N untyped) outbreaks: United States 4 and Peru 1. United States dairy cattle avian influenza: dairy herds have reported 951 (23) outbreaks across 16 states since March last year, mainly concentrated recently in California. Human infections from cattle: at least 8,500 cases monitored, 170 tested, and 40 positive (conjunctivitis, respiratory and influenza-like symptoms). Other derived outbreaks: infections in domestic cats, sheep and alpacas, among others, with fatal cases in cats. Wastewater surveillance: in week 4, 328 sampling sites provided test results, and H5-positive detections were found at 33 sampling sites in 5 states. Other updates: On 28 January, the United Kingdom reported one H5N1 infection in a person with long-term close contact with a farm with many sick birds; this is the first case in the country since 2022. The patient, from the West Midlands in central England, is doing well. The sick birds on the farm were infected with genotype DI.2, a virus known to circulate among birds in the country, which differs from the virus spreading among mammals and birds in the United States. No human-to-human transmission has been identified, and the risk to the general public is assessed as very low. Authorities recently added H5 avian influenza vaccine to the national stockpile. The US FDA updated pet food rules: pet foods made from meat, milk and eggs that are not heat-treated must include highly pathogenic avian influenza (mainly H5N1) in their food safety plans as a known or reasonably foreseeable hazard, to reduce the risk of infection from raw feeding. The USDA found a link between infections in turkeys and domestic cats in late December last year, and in January this year updated its surveillance policy to strengthen monitoring of highly pathogenic avian influenza in turkeys. In response to sporadic human infections with novel influenza A H5N1 virus during periods of increased seasonal influenza activity, the US CDC recommends shortening the time needed to subtype influenza A specimens from hospitalised patients, to reduce delays in differential diagnosis. Annual summary: Human cases: 2 H5N1 influenza cases (910 cumulative since 2003); most cases had prior exposure to susceptible animals. Avian and animal cases: 303 high- and low-pathogenic avian influenza outbreaks reported cumulatively in 29 countries. Assessment and recommendations: On 20 December, FAO, WHO and WOAH published a risk assessment for H5 influenza viruses. The H5 2.3.4.4b virus remains an avian virus; human cases mostly involved direct or indirect contact with susceptible animals, and there is no human-to-human transmission capability. Because the virus is widespread in wild and domestic animals, cases are expected to continue, and the global public health risk is assessed as low. The infection risk is low for the general public, and low to moderate for people who frequently handle contaminated animals or environments, depending mainly on the type and duration of exposure, protective measures and control measures. Countries are urged to strengthen surveillance of susceptible animals and high-risk groups.

i-ASK2FfhMQTPN3qUeINyA.zh: 疫情更新:  2025年第2週(1/6-1/12)全球陽性率約6.0%,陽性率以非洲區(13.9%)、美洲區(8.0%)及歐洲區(5.8%)為高。  WHO更新全球疫情資訊:  全球近28天(2024/11/11-12/8)期間,新增約20萬例病例及2,600餘例死亡,病例數及死亡數較前28天期間分別下降6%及24%;住院數及重症數分別新增約2.2萬例及2,000餘例,住院數及重症數較前28天期間分別下降1%及上升3%。 於2024年12月初(12/2-12/8),全球主要流行變異株XEC占比38.6%呈上升趨勢,其次為變異株KP.3.1.1占比33.2%呈下降趨勢。  評估與建議: 全球陽性率呈下降趨勢,其中,非洲區及西太平洋區呈上升趨勢,東南亞區上下波動,其他地區則呈下降趨勢。XEC為全球主要流行變異株,占比呈上升趨勢,惟尚未增加疾病嚴重度。WHO表示多數國家已將COVID-19納入常規呼吸道傳染病監測,建議各國提供民眾可負擔及可信賴的檢測、治療及疫苗,維持預警監視系統及持續追蹤變異株趨勢,並向WHO通報疫情資訊及維繫COVID-19期間所建立之基礎設施。
i-ASK2FfhMQTPN3qUeINyA.en: Epidemic update: In week 2 of 2025 (6–12 January), the global positivity rate was about 6.0%, highest in the African Region (13.9%), the Region of the Americas (8.0%) and the European Region (5.8%). WHO update on the global situation: In the past 28 days (11 November–8 December 2024), about 200,000 new cases and over 2,600 deaths were reported globally, a decrease of 6% in cases and 24% in deaths compared with the previous 28 days. About 22,000 new hospitalisations and over 2,000 new severe cases were reported; compared with the previous 28 days, hospitalisations fell 1% and severe cases rose 3%. In early December 2024 (2–8 December), the leading global circulating variant was XEC at 38.6%, with an upward trend, followed by KP.3.1.1 at 33.2%, with a downward trend. Assessment and recommendations: Global positivity is declining; it is rising in the African Region and the Western Pacific Region, fluctuating in the South-East Asia Region, and declining elsewhere. XEC is the main global circulating variant and its share is rising, but it has not yet increased disease severity. WHO notes that most countries have integrated COVID-19 into routine respiratory infection surveillance, and recommends that countries provide affordable and reliable testing, treatment and vaccines, maintain early warning and surveillance systems, continue tracking variant trends, report epidemic information to WHO, and maintain the infrastructure established during the COVID-19 period.

_bTLOBIo67LCx-3B4gREfQ.zh: 疫情更新:  2024年第52週(12/23-12/29)全球陽性率約4.3%,陽性率以非洲區(15.8%)、美洲區(9.2%)及歐洲區(3.6%)為高。 日本病例數持續上升,2024年第46-49週以KP.3.1.1變異株占比為高,其次為XEC變異株。 中國2024年12月疫情概況,新增112例重症及7例死亡,相較11月(35例重症/11例死亡)重症數上升而死亡數略降,新冠病毒陽性率略降且處低點,發燒門診就診量及類流感就診率呈上升趨勢,主要流行變異株為XDV、JN.1及其衍生變異株;香港2025年第2週(1/5-1/11)陽性率略降且處低點,JN.1及其衍生變異株爲主要流行變異株。  評估與建議: 全球陽性率近期下降,其中,非洲區上升,東地中海區上下波動,其他地區則呈持平或下降趨勢。XEC及KP.3.1.1為全球主要流行變異株,XEC變異株占比上升,惟尚未增加疾病嚴重度。WHO表示多數國家已將COVID-19納入常規呼吸道傳染病監測,建議各國提供民眾可負擔及可信賴的檢測、治療及疫苗,維持預警監視系統及持續追蹤變異株趨勢,並向WHO通報疫情資訊及維繫COVID-19期間所建立之基礎設施。
_bTLOBIo67LCx-3B4gREfQ.en: Epidemic update: In week 52 of 2024 (23–29 December), the global positivity rate was about 4.3%, highest in the African Region (15.8%), the Region of the Americas (9.2%) and the European Region (3.6%). Japan's case numbers continue to rise; in weeks 46–49 of 2024 the KP.3.1.1 variant accounted for the largest share, followed by XEC. China's COVID-19 situation in December 2024: 112 new severe cases and 7 deaths were reported, compared with 35 severe cases and 11 deaths in November. Severe case numbers rose while deaths fell slightly; the positivity rate declined slightly and is at a low point; fever clinic visits and influenza-like illness visit rates are rising. The main circulating variants in China are XDV, JN.1 and their derivatives. In Hong Kong, the positivity rate in week 2 of 2025 (5–11 January) declined slightly to a low point, and JN.1 and its derivatives are the main circulating variants. Assessment and recommendations: Global positivity has recently declined; it is rising in the African Region, fluctuating in the Eastern Mediterranean Region, and flat or declining elsewhere. 1jbsEYuSVmHqTZoFa6NZNA.en: Influenza-like illness (ILI) and acute respiratory infection (ARI) rates have risen recently in temperate regions of the Northern Hemisphere, with several countries above the threshold. Influenza is rising in Europe, Central America, Central and West Africa and several Asian countries; COVID-19 is at a low level; and RSV is rising in North America. In China, respiratory infectious disease activity has recently risen. Seasonal influenza activity in the north and south has continued to rise since late 2024, consistent with the trend in 2023. Influenza, RSV and human metapneumovirus (hMPV) infections are all rising, with influenza the main pathogen, and hMPV positivity is highest among children aged 5–14. COVID-19 is at a low level, but severe cases have risen, and authorities say medical resources remain within manageable limits. WHO notes that winter is the peak season for respiratory infections, and that respiratory infections and testing numbers are rising in many Northern Hemisphere countries, as expected. Because several respiratory pathogens are circulating at the same time, healthcare facilities in many countries are under a degree of strain. WHO recommends that the public take preventive measures and calls on countries to monitor respiratory pathogens.

ML7ZyAQWy12qgRb26F_H3w.en: Epidemic update: In week 49 of 2024 (2–8 December), the global positivity rate was about 13.5%, highest in the European Region (14.7%), the Region of the Americas (9.3%) and the African Region (7.9%). Japan's case numbers continue to rise: over 22,000 new cases were reported in week 51 (16–22 December), the fifth consecutive week of increase, and reported cases are higher than in the same period last year, with marked increases in Hokkaido, Tohoku and Kanto. In Tokyo Metropolis, KP.3 is the main variant, but the share of XEC is rising rapidly and is now over 40%. With the New Year holiday approaching in Japan, respiratory infections including COVID-19 and influenza are expected to keep rising. WHO global update: In the 28 days from 14 October to 10 November, over 200,000 new cases and 3,000 deaths were reported globally, a decrease of 39% in cases and 36% in deaths compared with the previous 28 days. Hospitalisations and severe cases increased by over 22,000 and 900 respectively; compared with the previous 28-day period, hospitalisations fell 15% and severe cases fell 24%. In mid-November (4–10 November), the main global circulating variants KP.3.1.1, XEC, JN.1 and KP.3 accounted for 45.6%, 28.4%, 13.1% and 7.7% respectively, and the XEC share was rising. On 23 December, WHO recommended that countries continue COVID-19 vaccination. As the virus keeps evolving, vaccine antigens should be updated to strengthen immune responses against current variants, and WHO recommends retaining monovalent JN.1-lineage variants as antigens in future vaccine formulations. Assessment and recommendations: Global positivity has recently risen slightly, with slight increases in the African, European and Western Pacific regions, and flat or declining trends elsewhere. KP.3.1.1 is the main global circulating variant; the XEC share is rising, but severity has not yet increased. WHO notes that most countries have integrated COVID-19 into routine respiratory infection surveillance, and recommends that countries provide affordable and reliable testing, treatment and vaccines, maintain early warning and surveillance systems, continue tracking variant trends, report epidemic information to WHO, and maintain the infrastructure established during the COVID-19 period.

Cv14MdEpMi-sQIZib4rAjw.en: Both Iberian countries have seen a marked increase in cases this year. As of 27 November, Spain had cumulatively reported 720 local and 133 imported cases, higher than the 255 local and 73 imported cases in 2023. The sharpest rise is among men aged 15–44, and sexual contact between men is suspected to be one of the causes of the epidemic. As of 1 December, Portugal had cumulatively reported 267 cases, 98 of which were related to sexual contact, with cases concentrated among men aged 20–49. Although the overall outbreak in the country has recently slowed, the southern Algarve region has reported a new outbreak, with 25 cases cumulatively, most of them children and adolescents.

h_Z9WKBXJrsiJPuHtk6MIQ.en:
Human cases: This week the United States reported 2 new H5 and 3 untyped cases, and Viet Nam reported 1 new human H5N1 infection.

Animal outbreaks (WAHIS): A total of 13 countries reported 248 new H5N1 outbreaks between 18 September and 4 December 2024: United States 87, Austria 51, Japan and Canada 29 each, Slovenia 12, Germany 10, Italy 9, Czechia 7, Hungary 5, Poland 3, and the Netherlands, United Kingdom and Croatia 2 each.

A total of 3 countries reported 5 new H5N5 outbreaks between 19 November and 2 December 2024: Iceland 3, and Norway and the United Kingdom 1 each.

Canada reported 1 new H5N2 outbreak on 16 November.

Colombia reported 1 new H5 (N untyped) outbreak on 20 November.

New Zealand reported 1 new H7N6 outbreak on 23 November.

US dairy cattle avian influenza:

Dairy farms: Since March this year, 15 states have reported a cumulative 718 (30) outbreaks, mainly concentrated in California recently.

Human exposure via cattle: At least 5,790 people have been cumulatively monitored and 147 tested, with 35 positive (conjunctivitis, respiratory and influenza-like symptoms).

Other derived outbreaks: Infections have been found in domestic cats, sheep, alpacas and others, with fatal cases reported in cats.

Wastewater surveillance: In week 47, 292 sampling sites provided test reports; H5-positive results were detected at 43 sampling sites in 2 states.

Other updates:

On 3 December, the California Department of Public Health announced a recall of all raw milk and cream products from Raw Fram, and since 27 November the farm has been under quarantine and sales restrictions. The company's production lines have repeatedly tested positive for avian influenza virus, and authorities advise consumers to avoid eating (or feeding pets) any raw milk products from Raw Fram.

On 3 December, the United Kingdom announced it had pre-purchased 5 million doses of H5 influenza vaccine from a domestic company, designed on current H5 virus strains, for immediate use if human transmission occurs, and had also pre-ordered vaccines targeting future pandemic strains. The United States, Japan and the EU have all activated stockpiled H5 vaccines.

Research published on 2 December compared ferret experiments with five H5N1 influenza viruses infecting different mammals since 2005 and a 2009 H1N1 influenza virus. Ferrets infected with more recent H5N1 viruses shed more infectious virus into the air than those infected with older viruses. This suggests that the current increase in H5N1 transmission may not necessarily be due to 'mammalian adaptation mutations' and may also result from higher viral shedding into the air.

Research published on 3 December found that an H5N1 human infection case reported by Australia in April this year (imported from India) was a reassortant virus of clade 2.3.2.1a, including gene segments from 2.3.2.1a, 2.3.4.4b and low-pathogenicity avian influenza in wild birds. Separately, H5N1 infections in India have spread to other countries, but few cases have been reported domestically, indicating data gaps caused by surveillance patterns in that country (or in South Asia). Authorities call on all sectors to continue monitoring HPAI H5 outbreaks in Asia.

vDK-MpJDOCP47khPQ1yhLQ.en:
The United States has an outbreak linked to cucumbers: as of 26 November, 68 cases have been reported from 19 states, at least 18 of whom were hospitalized, with no deaths. Most cases are in Montana, with onset dates between 12 October and 16 November. Investigations indicate the likely source is cucumbers produced in Mexico, and authorities have recalled suspected contaminated products.

Norway has an outbreak with 23 cases reported since mid-October, 8 of whom were hospitalized. Cases are spread across 9 regions of the country. Genetic sequencing shows the outbreak strains share a common source, which is possibly alfalfa sprouts. Authorities have recalled related products and advise people to avoid eating them.

Singapore reported that 24 children at an early childhood education centre had gastrointestinal symptoms, 7 of whom were hospitalized, and 3 were confirmed to be infected with Salmonella. The centre has taken multiple health protection measures, including suspending group activities and strengthening environmental disinfection.

2HpmDx5r5w30dFkbAo69bQ.en: WHO reports that as of 27 October this year, 33 countries have cumulatively reported more than 486,000 cases and over 4,000 deaths globally. Compared with the same period last year, cases decreased by 42% and deaths increased by 54%, respectively. Cases are concentrated in the Eastern Mediterranean Region, the African Region and the South-East Asia Region. Regional armed conflicts, natural disasters and other factors have reduced access to health care resources and intensified outbreaks. WHO is increasing production of oral cholera vaccine (OCV) to address the current vaccine shortage. WHO assesses the global risk of the outbreak as still very high.
