s-QF4KQNa-DaTgKia_rCzQ.en:
On 20 November, WHO approved Japan's LC16m8 vaccine for inclusion on its Emergency Use Listing (EUL). It can be used for people aged over 1 year, but is not applicable to pregnant women or immunocompromised groups. (The MVA-BN vaccine is currently available for people aged 12 years and over.)

On 22 November, WHO convened the second meeting of the IHR Emergency Committee on Mpox and stated that the Mpox outbreak continues to constitute a public health emergency of international concern (PHEIC). The committee's full report and updated recommendations will be released next week.

CuMysZ39qsPxVG2Pc2rP2A.en:
Human cases: The United States reported 8 new human infections.

Animal outbreaks (WAHIS): A total of 14 countries reported 151 new H5N1 outbreaks between 28 October 2020 and 21 November 2024: United States 77, Japan 19, Slovenia and Canada 11 each, Poland 9, Italy 6, United Kingdom 5, Spain 3, Germany, South Korea, Hungary and Turkey 2 each, and the Netherlands and France 1 each.

A total of 3 countries reported 8 new H5N5 outbreaks between 31 October and 13 November 2024: Norway 3, United Kingdom 3 and Iceland 2.

US dairy cattle avian influenza:

Dairy farms: Since March this year, 15 states have reported 612 (107) outbreaks; recent cases are mainly concentrated in California.

Human infection via cattle: At least 4,440 people have been monitored and 131 tested, with 31 positive (conjunctivitis, respiratory and influenza-like symptoms).

Other derived outbreaks: Infections in domestic cats, sheep, alpacas and others, with fatal cases in cats.

Wastewater surveillance: In week 45, 311 sampling sites provided test reports; H5-positive results were detected at 19 sampling sites in 3 states.

Other updates:

A US study published on 19 November compared H5N1 viruses from Viet Nam in 2004 (A/Vietnam/1203/2004, VN1203) and the United States in 2024 (A/Bovine/Ohio/B24osu-342/2024, Bov342). Both were lethal to mice. The former was confined to the respiratory tract, whereas the latter caused central nervous system inflammation in addition to respiratory symptoms.

US information updated on 18 November indicates that recent cases were all farm workers with mild illness, showing conjunctivitis or mild upper respiratory symptoms. The virus in the Washington State H5 case carried the NA-S247N mutation, which may slightly reduce susceptibility to neuraminidase inhibitors but is unlikely to affect clinical treatment outcomes. The virus in the California H5N1 case carried the PA-I38M mutation, which may slightly reduce susceptibility to cap-dependent endonuclease inhibitors (baloxavir marboxil); however, this drug is not currently a recommended treatment for H5N1.

Pennsylvania has no avian influenza outbreaks in cattle, but announced that from 26 November it would step up testing of bulk milk at dairy processing plants to prevent the spread of avian influenza. States that have taken similar measures despite having no outbreaks include Arkansas, Massachusetts and Oklahoma.

sVHe3WGbG4C-knzLtCaBZA.en:
Human cases: Canada reported 1 new H5N1 infection, and China reported 7 new H9N2 human infections.

Animal outbreaks (WAHIS): A total of 19 countries reported 128 new H5N1 outbreaks between 15 October and 14 November 2024: United States and Hungary 46 each, Germany 5, Italy, Czechia and France 4 each, Poland and Japan 3 each, Taiwan and Turkey 2 each, and Romania, Portugal, Switzerland, Slovakia, Ukraine, Hong Kong, United Kingdom, Bulgaria and Canada 1 each.

France reported 3 new H5 (N untyped) outbreaks between 1 and 13 November 2024.

Canada reported 1 new H5N2 outbreak on 31 October 2024.

The United Kingdom reported 1 new H5N5 outbreak on 4 November 2024.

US dairy cattle avian influenza:

Dairy farms: Since March this year, 15 states have reported 505 (59) outbreaks; recent cases are mainly concentrated in California and Utah.

Human infection via cattle: At least 4,010 people have been monitored and 121 tested, with 25 positive (conjunctivitis, respiratory and influenza-like symptoms).

Other derived outbreaks: Infections in domestic cats, sheep, alpacas and others, with fatal cases in cats.

Wastewater surveillance: In week 44, 324 sampling sites provided test reports; H5-positive results were detected at 14 sampling sites in 1 state.

Other updates:

A preprint study published on 2 November found that older people born in certain years had higher resistance to H5N1 virus, possibly because they were exposed to H1N1 and H2N2 viruses in childhood. After H5N1 vaccination, both younger and older groups produced H5-reactive antibodies, with young children showing higher seroconversion rates, suggesting that vaccinating younger groups may be more effective during an outbreak.

A preprint study published on 5 November reported that all 16 H5N1 human cases in Cambodia between February 2023 and August 2024 were caused by clade 2.3.2.1c, and 14 of them were reassortant viruses of clades 2.3.2.1c and 2.3.4.4b. This is presumed to be a possible reason for the recurrence of outbreaks in the country and also highlights the persistent outbreak threat in Southeast Asia.

A study published on 11 November reported that since 2022, several South American countries have had HPAI H5N1 outbreaks in marine mammals. The study found that the viruses largely carry the same mammalian adaptation mutations and have spilled back into terns. Cases of mammal-to-mammal transmission of H5N1 have already occurred in North American dairy farms, European fur farms and South American marine wildlife, a warning sign that should not be ignored.

On 7 November, Oahu, Hawaii, United States detected H5 virus in wastewater for the first time; the source of the virus cannot yet be confirmed. The state has reported no human or animal cases, and authorities say the risk to the public remains low but encourage precautionary measures.

HIy8yoAQ6Xph9NNjUZFffQ.en:
Situation update: In week 43 of 2024 (28 October–3 November), the global positivity rate was about 16.5%, highest in the European Region (17.8%), the Region of the Americas (13.0%) and the African Region (5.0%).

China reported COVID-19 infection data for October, with 57 new severe cases and 6 deaths. Fever clinic visits and the proportion of influenza-like illness cases at sentinel hospitals have remained stable recently, and COVID-19 positivity is at a low level. XDV and JN.1 are the main circulating variants in the country. Hong Kong's indicators are at low levels, with JN.1-derived variants the main circulating strains.

EU countries have shown a continuing downward trend since their July peak. Positivity at sentinel hospitals is lower than the same period last year or stable, cases are still mainly among people aged 65 and over, and KP.3 is the main circulating variant recently, accounting for about 60%.

Other updates:

An MMWR report published on 7 November found that the US CDC conducted serological surveys in Michigan and Colorado between June and August. Of 115 dairy plant workers, 8 (7%) showed serological evidence of recent infection. The work of all 8 cases was related to milking, and 4 of them said their illness began within a few days before or after the cows fell ill.

On 1 November the US CDC updated a summary of a recent study. In the study using a human virus sample from Texas (A/Texas/37/2024), direct contact transmission between ferrets was 100%, and transmission via respiratory route or contaminated surfaces was 66%. All infected ferrets became severely ill and died. These results are consistent with those for a Spanish mink and a Chilean human virus sample, but differ from those for a human virus sample from Michigan. The Texas virus also has more mammalian-adaptation features (PB2 E627K and K142E), and the country will conduct a further IRAT assessment.

DRwKPSeIZeXl4zU51CLLCw.en:
Since May 2022 and as of 1 November this year, 127 (1*) countries/territories have cumulatively reported 114,594 confirmed cases globally, including at least 241 deaths (CFR: 0.2%).

As of week 44 this year, 79 countries/territories have cumulatively reported 21,193 confirmed cases globally: African Region 10,743 (1,382 this week), Region of the Americas 5,872 (201), Western Pacific Region 2,010 (82), European Region 1,572 (13), Eastern Mediterranean Region 773 (0), and South-East Asia Region 223 (0).

A preprint study on 24 October found that the Ia outbreak in Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo, and the Ib outbreak in South Kivu both show a certain proportion of APOBEC3-type mutations in viral genes. The researchers judge that this wave of Ia cases is linked to human-to-human transmission rather than multiple independent animal-to-human transmission events, and that its epidemiological characteristics are still evolving.

On 10 October the US reported a second cluster with resistance to the treatment drug tecovirimat (TPOXX). It differs from the first resistant cluster identified in California in 2022: this cluster involves multiple states, and its cases had no treatment history. The study considers that the transmission and prevalence of antiviral drug resistance may currently be underestimated, and recommends strengthened sequencing and surveillance, as well as improved healthcare workers' adherence to antiviral use and clinical guidelines to reduce the occurrence of resistance.

WHO approved the use of the Jynneos vaccine for adolescents aged 12 to 17 on 14 October.
